options: Automatically sends an email whenever a task in the DAG fails, no custom code required
Prevents a task from ever failing
Only works for DAGs scheduled hourly
Requires writing a custom Python callback function
questions.explain: email_on_failure is a built-in flag — set it to True and Airflow handles sending the email automatically via its configured SMTP connection.

questions.q: What does `on_failure_callback` let you do that `email_on_failure` doesn't?
options: Run any custom Python function on failure, with full access to context like task, DAG, run, and log URL
Send emails faster than email_on_failure
Prevent retries from happening
Nothing — they do exactly the same thing
questions.explain: on_failure_callback runs your own function, giving full flexibility (like posting to Slack) with rich failure context, unlike the fixed email-only behavior of email_on_failure.

questions.q: What information does the `context` dict passed to a failure callback include?
options: Which task, which DAG, which run, and a direct link to the log
Only the current server time
The entire Airflow source code
Nothing useful — it's an empty object
questions.explain: The context dict gives a callback everything needed to build a specific, actionable alert, including a direct log URL.

questions.q: Why put `on_failure_callback` inside `default_args` instead of on each task individually?
options: It applies the callback to every task in the DAG automatically, avoiding repetition
default_args is required by Airflow and has no other purpose
It makes tasks run faster
Individual task callbacks are not supported by Airflow at all
questions.explain: default_args lets you configure a setting once at the DAG level instead of repeating it on every single task.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does alerting matter even if a pipeline already has good visibility (logs, Task Instances)?
options: Visibility alone still requires a human to remember to go check it — alerting closes that loop automatically
Visibility features don't actually work without alerting enabled
Alerting replaces the need for logs entirely
It doesn't matter — visibility alone is always sufficient
questions.explain: A pipeline can fail silently even with great visibility tools, if nobody proactively checks — alerting makes the pipeline surface problems on its own.
